the generation of S‐layer variants in C. fetus, and the role that these variants may play in persistent mucosal colonization and the pathogenesis of C. fetus infections.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sapA mutagenized C. fetus strains undergo high‐frequency generation and selection of antigenic variants.
sapA antigenic variation is a high‐frequency process, which involves the generation of multiple variants and that the mechanism of variation is DNA reciprocal recombination.
the sapA gene family of C. fetus is a reservoir for antigenic variation and is a major factor in the pathogenesis of this species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the C. fetus S‐layer proteins, like those of other bacteria, are highly variable, and that the mechanisms of variation in C. fetus are more similar to those of the Streptococcus and Neisseria species, than to those of the Borrelia species.

(1) sapA gene targeting by km insertion causes the loss of S‐layer proteins, (2) km insertion is associated with a truncated 50 kDa S‐layer protein that is not exported to the surface, (3) the km marker is lost during sapA gene rearrangement and (4) the resulting sapA mutants are serum sensitive and are attenuated for virulence in mice.
